blocks.text: A network driver decides what network namespace and connectivity a container gets; bridge (private IP behind NAT on one host) is the default and covers almost every single-host case.

rows: Own netns, veth into a Linux bridge, private IP, NAT out
Subnets can clash with VPN/LAN ranges
Host's netns: no isolation, no NAT
`-p` ignored; port clashes; native only on Linux
Jobs that must not reach the network

items: Docker creates a Linux bridge (`docker0` default, `br-<id>` user-defined).
Each container gets a veth pair: `eth0` inside, the other end on the bridge.
Outbound traffic is masqueraded to the host IP.
Published ports add DNAT rules (plus docker-proxy for some paths such as localhost).

blocks.text: Default pools start at 172.17.0.0/16. If your office VPN uses the same range, containers lose access to it. Set `default-address-pools` in daemon.json.

Q: "bridge vs host networking?" A: "bridge gives each container its own network namespace and private IP behind NAT, with ports published explicitly; host shares the host's namespace, with no isolation, no NAT and no -p, trading isolation for performance and simplicity. It's native only on Linux."
